name: Rotunda Masjid
summary: A domed circular prayer hall is viewed at an angle, with a curved terracotta side wall and a rounded rear minaret.
why: The dome centers on x=55 and overlaps the drum between y=43 and47. The drum uses matching 19-by-7 elliptical top and bottom faces, joined by vertical walls. The rear minaret overlaps the drum by one unit at x=36–37. The entrance faces left at x=46.5, while the side window sits on the curved right wall; this deliberate offset describes depth rather than a misaligned frontal facade.
risk: The rotunda is a contemporary mosque interpretation rather than a specific monument. The colored side plane conveys the oblique view most clearly; monochrome keeps its rounded foundation and rear minaret.
sub1: Curved walls replace a flat facade
sub2: Domed roof, drum, and rounded base align
reasonToChoose: You want a mosque with architectural depth and a softer footprint.
